concepts.name: Constitutional Basis and Status of GST Council
key_dimensions: Article 279A inserted by 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 — not an ordinary statutory body
GST Council as a constitutional body vs. quasi-judicial body distinction
Supreme Court's ruling in Union of India vs. Mohit Minerals (2022) — recommendations are persuasive, not binding
Cooperative federalism vs. coercive federalism debate arising from this judgment

concepts.name: Composition and Membership of GST Council
key_dimensions: Union Finance Minister as Chairperson; Union Minister of State (Finance) as member
Each state's Finance Minister (or nominated minister) as members — all 28 states + 8 UTs with legislature
UTs without legislature (e.g., Ladakh, Dadra & Nagar Haveli) — representation mechanism and distinction
Trap: J&K and Delhi/Puducherry have legislatures, so their ministers sit as members, not nominees

concepts.name: Voting Weights and Decision-Making Mechanism
key_dimensions: Centre carries 1/3rd of total votes; all states together carry 2/3rd of total votes
3/4th majority required for every decision — no simple majority provisions
Each state has equal weight (1 vote regardless of size/population) — contrast with Rajya Sabha representation
Trap: Quorum requirement — 50% of total membership must be present; Centre's veto arithmetic

concepts.name: Scope of GST Council's Recommendations
key_dimensions: Taxes, cesses, and surcharges to be subsumed under GST
Goods and services exempt from GST; threshold limits of turnover
GST rates including floor rates with bands; special rates for calamities/disasters
Model GST laws, principles of levy, apportionment of IGST; place of supply rules

concepts.name: Goods Outside GST Purview — Excluded Items
key_dimensions: Five petroleum products: crude oil, high-speed diesel, motor spirit (petrol), natural gas, aviation turbine fuel (ATF) — to be included only when Council recommends
Alcohol for human consumption — entirely outside GST, remains with states
Electricity — outside GST; stamp duty and property tax also excluded
Trap: Petroleum products are 'within' GST framework constitutionally but zero-rated until Council decides — often confused with alcohol which is permanently outside

concepts.name: IGST Model and Apportionment Mechanism
key_dimensions: IGST levied by Centre on inter-state supply of goods/services under Article 269A
IGST revenue shared between Centre and states — Parliament determines apportionment
Destination-based principle: tax flows to consuming state, not producing state
Mohit Minerals case: States can levy IGST on ocean freight — federal jurisdiction overlap issue

concepts.name: GST Compensation Mechanism and the 5-Year Guarantee
key_dimensions: States guaranteed 14% annual revenue growth over 2015-16 base year for 5 years (ended June 2022)
GST Compensation Cess levied on sin/luxury goods to fund the shortfall
COVID-19 controversy: Centre offered states borrowing options instead of direct compensation — federal fiscal tension
Post-2022 status: Cess extended to repay back-to-back loans but no longer for state compensation — important distinction

concepts.name: GST Compensation Cess — Structure and Controversy
key_dimensions: Levied on specific goods (tobacco, pan masala, aerated drinks, luxury cars, coal) under GST Compensation to States Act, 2017
Cess is over and above the peak GST rate of 28% on demerit goods
Extended beyond June 2022 to repay Centre's borrowings made on states' behalf — states' grievance
Trap: Cess revenue does NOT go to Consolidated Fund of India — goes to GST Compensation Fund; distinct from surcharges

concepts.name: Dual GST Structure: CGST, SGST, IGST, and UTGST
key_dimensions: CGST (Centre) and SGST (State) levied simultaneously on intra-state supply — concurrent jurisdiction
UTGST applicable in UTs without legislature (e.g., Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, Ladakh) — Centre collects both CGST and UTGST
IGST on inter-state supply and imports — only Centre can levy
Trap: For UTs with legislature (Delhi, Puducherry, J&K), SGST applies, not UTGST

concepts.name: Input Tax Credit (ITC) Mechanism under GST
key_dimensions: Seamless ITC across the value chain — eliminates cascading tax effect (tax on tax)
ITC restrictions: blocked credits on motor vehicles, food, health services, construction (Section 17(5))
IGST ITC utilization order: first against IGST, then CGST, then SGST — asymmetric utilization rules
Fake ITC frauds and GST portal's invoice-matching mechanism (GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B mismatch issues)

concepts.name: GST Rate Structure and the Rate Slabs
key_dimensions: Four main rate slabs: 5%, 12%, 18%, 28% — plus zero-rated (0%) and exempt categories
28% slab + compensation cess on sin/luxury goods; essential goods at 0% or 5%
GST Council's role in rate rationalization — recommendations of rate rationalization committee (2024)
Trap: Zero-rated supply (exports + SEZ) allows ITC refund; exempt supply does NOT — critical distinction

concepts.name: Dispute Resolution Mechanism within GST Council
key_dimensions: Article 279A(11): GST Council to establish mechanism to adjudicate disputes between Centre and states or among states
No dispute resolution body has been formally constituted yet — constitutional lacuna in practice
Mohit Minerals judgment: Courts can review Council's recommendations if they violate constitutional provisions
Comparison with Finance Commission's dispute role — different mandate and authority

concepts.name: GST and Fiscal Federalism — Centre-State Financial Relations
key_dimensions: States surrendered their exclusive tax domains (VAT, octroi, entry tax) — asymmetric sacrifice argument
Centre surrendered central excise and service tax — but retained larger administrative machinery
15th Finance Commission's interaction with GST revenue projections and devolution
Vertical imbalance argument: States collect ~half of GST but have larger expenditure responsibilities

concepts.name: GST Network (GSTN) — Technology Backbone
key_dimensions: GSTN is a not-for-profit, non-government company — Section 8 company; government shareholding increased to 100% in 2018 (originally private majority)
Functions: taxpayer registration, invoice upload, return filing, tax payment, ITC matching
GSTN ≠ GST Council — GSTN is the IT infrastructure; Council is the policy-making constitutional body
Trap: GSTN is not a statutory body or constitutional body — it is a special purpose vehicle (SPV)

concepts.name: Composition Scheme under GST
key_dimensions: Available to businesses with turnover up to ₹1.5 crore (₹75 lakh for special category states) — pay flat rate, no ITC
Service providers (except restaurant services) excluded from composition scheme
Composition taxpayers cannot collect GST from customers or make inter-state supplies
Trap: Composition scheme threshold for service providers is ₹50 lakh under QRMP/special composition — different from goods

concepts.name: Special Category States and GST Threshold Variations
key_dimensions: Special category states (NE states + Uttarakhand, HP, J&K) have lower thresholds: ₹10 lakh for services (vs ₹20 lakh general)
Threshold for goods registration: ₹40 lakh general; ₹20 lakh for special category states
Council's power to set differential thresholds for different states — asymmetric federalism in action
Trap: Special category status for GST purposes ≠ special category status for Finance Commission purposes — different lists

concepts.name: GST on Services — Significant Sectoral Issues
key_dimensions: Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM): recipient pays GST instead of supplier (e.g., legal services, GTA)
Exemptions: healthcare, education (up to higher secondary), government services — but private coaching taxable
Online gaming, casinos, horse racing brought under 28% GST (October 2023 Council decision) — major policy shift
Trap: Export of services is zero-rated (eligible for ITC refund), but intermediary services are taxable in India — place of supply confusion

concepts.name: 101st Constitutional Amendment — Key Provisions and Limitations
key_dimensions: Amended Articles 246, 248, 269; inserted Articles 246A, 269A, 279A; amended Sixth Schedule entries
Article 246A: Concurrent power to both Parliament and state legislatures to legislate on GST — novel concurrent taxation
Parliament retains exclusive power over IGST (inter-state supply) — states cannot legislate on inter-state GST
Trap: 101st Amendment did NOT repeal Article 246 or the Seventh Schedule — entries 84 (Union) and 54 (State) were amended, not deleted

concepts.name: Anti-Profiteering Provisions under GST
key_dimensions: Section 171 of CGST Act: Businesses must pass on ITC benefits/rate reduction benefits to consumers
National Anti-Profiteering Authority (NAA) — sunset clause, merged with Competition Commission of India (CCI) in 2022
NAA investigated FMCG, real estate, restaurant sectors — penalties include 10% fine on profiteered amount
Trap: Anti-profiteering is a CGST Act provision, not directly part of GST Council's constitutional mandate under Article 279A — legislative vs. constitutional distinction

concepts.name: GST and E-Commerce Operators — Tax Collection at Source (TCS)
key_dimensions: E-commerce operators (Amazon, Flipkart) required to collect 1% TCS on net taxable supplies made through their platform
Mandatory registration for e-commerce operators regardless of turnover threshold — no threshold exemption
Operators liable to pay GST on certain services (e.g., passenger transport, accommodation) even if underlying supplier is unregistered
Trap: TCS under GST is different from TCS under Income Tax Act — different rates, different legal basis, often confused in questions
